title: Modular elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem

definitions.statement: E/Q is modular if there exists a weight 2 newform f in S_2(Gamma_0(N)) such that L(E, s) = L(f, s).

definitions.term: Deformation Ring R and Hecke Algebra T
definitions.statement: Universal deformation ring R of residual Galois representation rho_{E,p} and Hecke algebra T acting on cusp forms.
The canonical surjective homomorphism phi: R -> T is an isomorphism of complete intersection rings.

theorems.label: Wiles Modularity Theorem (Semistable)
theorems.statement: Every semistable elliptic curve over Q is modular (Wiles 1995). Extended to all E/Q by Breuil-Conrad-Diamond-Taylor (2001).

theorems.label: Analytic Continuation & Functional Equation of L(E,s)
theorems.statement: Because E is modular, L(E, s) extends to an entire function on C and satisfies Lambda(E, s) = w_E Lambda(E, 2-s) with w_E = +-1.

theorems.label: Fermat's Last Theorem
theorems.statement: x^n + y^n = z^n has no non-zero integer solutions for n >= 3 (Frey-Ribet-Wiles).

conjectures.label: Fontaine-Mazur Conjecture
conjectures.statement: Every geometric Galois representation comes from algebraic geometry / automorphic forms.

open_gaps: Modularity guarantees that L(E, s) is defined at s=1 and differentiable, enabling BSD to be rigorously posed, but does not prove rank equality ord_{s=1} L(E, s) = rank E(Q) for r >= 2.
computational_handles: Fourier coefficient a_n(f) computation of weight 2 modular forms.
Sign of functional equation w_E = -a_N(E) or root number computation.
High-precision order of vanishing determination at s=1.

citations.ref: Wiles, A. (1995). Modular elliptic curves and Fermat's Last Theorem, Ann. of Math., 141, 443-551.
